study_identification.title: Molecular and micro-architectural mapping of gray matter alterations in psychosis

study_characteristics.study_objective: To characterize the molecular and micro-architectural attributes that underlie the pattern of cortical atypical maturation in different psychosis-related groups by computing centiles from regional volumes and mapping them to 46 different neurobiological features including neurotransmitters, cell types, layer thickness, microstructure, cortical expansion, and metabolism.

dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (UK Biobank; ABCD; B-SNIP; ASRB; LA5c; MCIC; PAFIP; ALSPAC; and other studies)

hc_n.answer: 38,696 (38,232 for chronic group HC; 195 for FEP group HC; 269 for PE group HC)

hc_age.answer: Overall: mean 51.91, sd 23.68, min 9.76, max 81.82; Chronic group HC (n=38,232): mean 51.91±23.68, min 9.76, max 81.82; FEP group HC (n=195): mean 30.64±7.66, min 16.78, max 52.80; PE group HC (n=269): mean 22.30±1.46, min 19.78, max 24.78

imaging_modality.answer: T1-weighted MRI; T2-weighted MRI (available for some datasets)

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: FreeSurfer v6.0; FreeSurfer v6.0.0; FreeSurfer v6.0.1; Desikan-Killiany (DK) atlas parcellation; volumetric measurements for each region-of-interest

quality_checking_detail.answer: Quality control procedures were implemented to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the derived cerebral volumes. Thirteen HC subjects exhibiting significant artifacts or processing errors were excluded from further analysis. Sensitivity analyses conducted using the Euler index as a proxy for image quality to evaluate the stability of centile estimations. Centiles are highly robust to variations in image quality as noted in Bethlehem et al. 2022 Supplemental Material.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: GAMLSS-based centile method accounts for site-effects through out-of-sample alignment using maximum likelihood to estimate study-specific offsets (random effects) for three moments of the underlying statistical distributions: mean (μ), variance (σ), and skewness (ν) in an age- and sex-specific manner. This allows computation of centiles for each scan in a new study on the same scale as the reference population curve while accounting for study-specific 'batch effects'. The normative model was trained on ~120,000 participants from 100 different studies (Bethlehem et al. 2022).

model_origin_detail.answer: BrainChart reference GAMLSS models trained on approximately 120,000 participants from 100 different studies spanning the lifespan from 17 post-conception weeks to 100 years. Models are age-normed and sex-stratified, providing measures of brain structure atypicalities across the lifespan. See Bethlehem et al., Nature, 2022 (https://github.com/brainchart/Lifespan) for details of the normative cohort.

modeling_method.answer: GAMLSS (Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape)

software_tool.answer: Lifespan Brain Chart models (https://github.com/brainchart/Lifespan); GAMLSS R package (Stasinopoulos & Rigby, 2007)

response_variable.answer: Regional cortical gray matter volumes (34 Desikan-Killiany regions, averaged across hemispheres)

predictor_effects.answer: Age and Sex are modeled as fixed effects in the normative curves. Site/Scanner effects are modeled as random effects (study-specific offsets for mean, variance, and skewness) using out-of-sample alignment approach.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The GAMLSS normative modeling approach explicitly handles multiple nuisance structures: (1) Site/scanner effects are handled through study-specific random effect offsets for mean (μ), variance (σ), and skewness (ν); (2) Age nonlinearity is captured through generalized additive modeling; (3) Sex effects are handled through sex-stratified models; (4) Heteroscedasticity across age is modeled through the scale parameter; (5) Skewness in the distribution is modeled through the shape parameter. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to verify robustness to image quality (Euler index). The method is described as highly robust to variations in image quality.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: This model, available at https://github.com/brainchart/Lifespan, estimated cross-sectional normative age-related trends from 100 different studies (around 120,000 participants; see Supplementary Information in [20] for details of the normative cohort, pages 120-151). Therefore, age-normed and sex-stratified measures of brain structure atypicalities across the lifespan, known as centiles (Fig. 1A), could be derived for each psychosis-related and HC individual in our cohorts... The out-of-sample centile method used here enabled us to calculate centiles without the need to re-train the model on the ~120,000 subjects used for the original normative curves [37]. Briefly, our out-of-sample data is aligned to the corresponding epoch of the normative trajectory, using maximum likelihood to estimate the study specific offsets (random effects) for three moments of the underlying statistical distributions: mean (μ), variance (σ), and skewness (ν) in an age- and sex-specific manner. This allows to compute centiles for each scan in a new study, on the same scale as the reference population curve, while accounting for study-specific 'batch effects'. Additionally, centiles are highly robust to variations in image quality (see Supplemental Material of [20]). Nevertheless, sensitivity analyses were conducted using the Euler index as a proxy for image quality to evaluate the stability of centile estimations.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.location: Main text page 1289, lines 56-59; Supplementary Methods page 96-97

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study uses a pre-trained normative model from Bethlehem et al. 2022, and does not perform validation within the same domain using non-independent data. The focus is on applying the pre-trained model to new clinical cohorts.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: Not applicable - study uses pre-trained normative model.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: While the study does not explicitly validate the normative model on independent same-domain data, it performs sensitivity analyses that serve as indirect validation: (1) Leave-one-study-out cross-validation within the chronic group and SCZ diagnosis to verify centiles and loadings are not primarily influenced by individual studies (Supplementary Figs. 12-13); (2) Euler index sensitivity analysis to verify robustness to image quality variations (Supplementary Fig. 5); (3) Global centile correction sensitivity analysis (Supplementary Fig. 4). These analyses provide evidence of model stability across different subsets of data, though they are not formal independent validation.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: Leave-one-study-out cross-validation performed both within the chronic group and SCZ diagnosis indicated that centiles and loadings were not primarily influenced by individual studies (Supplementary Figs. 12 and 13, respectively)... sensitivity analyses were conducted using the Euler index as a proxy for image quality to evaluate the stability of centile estimations.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.location: Main text page 1292, lines 109-110; page 1289, lines 59-60

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study does not validate the normative model on data from a different domain (e.g., different imaging modalities, different populations beyond neuroimaging). The validation activities described are all within the neuroimaging domain using T1-weighted MRI data from different cohorts, which constitute same-domain validation.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: No explicit validation on different domain datasets is described in the paper.

clinical_dataset.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset: ABCD (n=2 SCZ); ASRB (n=257 SCZ); B-SNIP (n=100 SCZ, n=62 SAD, n=96 SCZ-relatives, n=64 SAD-relatives); LA5c (n=48 SCZ); MCIC (n=104 SCZ); UKB (n=14 SCZ); PAFIP (n=352 FEP); ALSPAC (n=48 PE-suspected, n=73 PE-definite, n=36 PE-clinical)

diseases_studied.answer: Schizophrenia (SCZ); Schizoaffective Disorder (SAD); First Episode Psychosis (FEP); Psychotic Experiences (PE); First-degree relatives of SCZ and SAD patients (SCZ-relatives, SAD-relatives)

clinical_groups_n.answer: SCZ:525; SAD:62; FEP:352; PE-suspected:48; PE-definite:73; PE-clinical:36; SCZ-relatives:96; SAD-relatives:64

clinical_groups_age.answer: SCZ: mean 37.63±12.06, min 10.19, max 77.82; SAD: mean 33.77±10.78, min 11.68, max 57.06; FEP: mean 31.43±8.78, min 18.78, max 59.81; PE-suspected: mean 21.55±1.06, min 20.78, max 24.78; PE-definite: mean 21.75±1.59, min 19.78, max 24.78; PE-clinical: mean 20.89±0.92, min 19.78, max 23.78; SCZ-relatives: mean 43.75±15.25, min 11.68, max 65.07; SAD-relatives: mean 40.00±16.20, min 11.68, max 65.07

deviation_metric.answer: Centile scores (ranging from 0 to 1, with values below 0.5 indicating lower GM volume than expected normative values for age and sex after adjusting for scanning site offset). Extreme deviations defined as centile < 0.05. Effect sizes (Cohen's d) computed between regional centiles of each pair of groups.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Statistical linking of centile deviations to clinical groups: (1) Wilcoxon rank-sum test to compare regional centiles of each diagnosis/group with HC, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across brain regions; (2) Effect sizes (Cohen's d) computed between regional centiles for each pair of groups; (3) Sum of Squared Differences (SSD) between groups with permutation testing (10,000 permutations) to assess statistical significance; (4) PCA-CCA multivariate modeling to map 46 neurobiological features to centiles, with spin test for spatial autocorrelation-preserving permutation testing; (5) Bootstrap sampling (1000 samples) to estimate standard errors of model weights; (6) Pearson correlation between neurobiological maps and dimensionally-reduced predicted centiles to compute loadings; (7) Neurobiological similarity matrix correlated with structural co-vulnerability to psychosis matrix (spin-tested); (8) Leave-one-study-out cross-validation within chronic group and SCZ diagnosis.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: All psychosis-related groups showed significantly decreased global GM volume centiles compared to HC, with greater impact on clinically diagnosed individuals (FEP and chronic); neurobiological features (particularly metabolism and neurotransmitter concentrations) were highly co-localized with centile deviations, supporting the regional vulnerability hypothesis.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Centile analysis revealed significantly decreased global GM volume across all psychosis-related groups (relatives P=0.0021; PE P=0.0124; FEP P<10^-7; chronic P<10^-28), with greater impact on more severe conditions. SCZ showed significantly reduced centiles for all regions, while FEP exhibited significant differences in all regions except inferior temporal and temporal pole. Relatives showed reduced centiles in association cortices (cingulate, temporal, frontal). PE-clinical group exhibited 11 significantly reduced regions, while PE-suspected and PE-definite showed no significant differences. All pairs of groups showed significant differences in centile distributions (P_perm<0.005) except relatives vs. PE (SSD=0.054, P_perm=0.166). PCA-CCA modeling revealed significant associations between neurobiological features and centiles for all groups except PE (FDR-corrected P_spin<0.05), with strongest correlations for FEP (r=0.63) and chronic (r=0.68). Most consistent negative loadings (indicating high presence of features in low-centile regions) included: neurotransmitters (5-HT1B, 5-HT2A, α4β2, NET, GABA), synapse density, and metabolism (CMRGlu, CBF, CMRO2). The correlation between neurobiological similarity and structural co-vulnerability matrices was significant (Pearson's r=0.21, P_spin<10^-6), indicating that regions with similar neurobiological attributes tend to exhibit comparable vulnerabilities across psychotic conditions.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Several limitations noted: (1) Psychotic disorders were grouped with varying sample sizes and diagnoses, resulting in heterogeneous groups, though SCZ and SAD are considered neuropsychologically indistinguishable and show overlapping GM reduction patterns; (2) Antipsychotic medication may impact cortical volume in chronic individuals, while relatives, PE, and FEP are not influenced by medication; (3) Normative models only available for cortical brain volume averaged across hemispheres (not subcortical volume, cortical thickness, or surface area) due to computational requirements; (4) Risk of overfitting in CCA with limited sample size (34 regions), though mitigated by PCA dimensionality reduction and confirmed with PLS analysis; (5) Neurobiological data derived from normative non-psychotic individuals rather than individuals with schizophrenia; (6) Loadings reported instead of weights, though both showed high resemblance.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The centile-based approach provides a standardized and interpretable metric for detecting alterations in regional volumes, contributing to identification of patterns of atypical neuroanatomical maturation across psychiatric disorders. Results support a continuum view of psychosis psychopathology, as the number of significantly affected regions increased with disorder severity. The significant co-localization of neurobiological features with abnormal GM trajectories sheds light on vulnerability factors that may underlie atypical brain maturation during different stages of psychosis, which could help define subtypes for future imaging-first molecular phenotyping. The method accounts for age-, sex-, and site-effects through the GAMLSS normative modeling framework with study-specific random effect offsets.

general_notes.general_notes: This study uses the BrainChart lifespan normative models developed by Bethlehem et al. (2022, Nature) which span from 17 post-conception weeks to 100 years and are trained on ~120,000 participants from 100 studies. The full list of datasets used for HC is: ABCD (n=8,762; F=4,500), ASRB (n=177; F=92), B-SNIP (n=93; F=59), LA5c (n=121; F=57), MCIC (n=90; F=28), UKB (n=28,989; F=14,403), PAFIP (n=195; F=75), ALSPAC (n=269; F=154). For clinical groups: ABCD (n=2 SCZ; F=1), ASRB (n=257 SCZ; F=76), B-SNIP (n=100 SCZ/F=30, n=62 SAD/F=37, n=96 SCZ-relatives/F=68, n=64 SAD-relatives/F=43), LA5c (n=48 SCZ; F=11), MCIC (n=104 SCZ; F=25), UKB (n=14 SCZ; F=5), PAFIP (n=352 FEP; F=138), ALSPAC (n=48 PE-suspected/F=33, n=73 PE-definite/F=42, n=36 PE-clinical/F=28). The PCA-CCA multivariate approach mapped 46 neurobiological features to centiles, classified under six types: neurotransmitter (19 features), cell type (7), layer thickness (6), microstructure (5), cortical expansion (4), and metabolism (5). Neurobiological maps were obtained from neuromaps toolbox (https://github.com/netneurolab/neuromaps) and parcellated according to Desikan-Killiany atlas. Spin test was used for spatial autocorrelation-preserving permutation testing (10,000 rotations). Analysis code available at https://github.com/RafaelRomeroGarcia/NeurobiologyCentilesPsychosis and https://github.com/RafaelRomeroGarcia/cca_pls_toolkit. Study approved by Ethical Committee of Clinical Investigation of Cantabria, Spain (ID: 2016.095) for PAFIP; other datasets have their own ethical approvals as described in supplementary materials.
